sources.title: Act 8 boss counter discussion • community reports

phases.name: Armor loop
phases.text: Knock Cerastes down to damage Leg Armor; hit his Block or bypass/break Auto-Block to damage Shield Armor; connect the final hit of your Striker to damage Spirit Armor. Damaging one armor type locks it until another armor type is damaged. Breaking all three creates the boss-generated Stun and your main damage window.

phases.name: Opening • 100–91%
phases.text: Armor repairs over time. If damaged armor fully repairs in this phase, it becomes Overcharged. Keep rotating the three armor interactions. During an Overdrive transition, land a Light or Medium intercept to remove Overdrive.

phases.name: Middle • 90–51%
phases.text: Armor begins with more durability. Hitting a locked armor type repairs it, so read the armor icons before repeating a knockdown, Block hit or Striker.

phases.name: Late • 50–6%
phases.text: Armor durability varies, and hitting locked armor can Overcharge it. External Stun no longer supplies the opening; use spacing and the Stun created by breaking all three armor types. Older footage that relied on Parry-Stun in this phase is not a dependable tactic.

phases.name: Finish • 5–0%
phases.text: At 5%, the armors Overcharge and ordinary attacks cannot damage Cerastes. Survive while his Health drains toward 1%. At 1%, strike Cerastes' Block with a Light Attack to trigger the encounter finish.

attackerProfile: A bound Striker is effectively part of the core armor rotation because Spirit Armor is damaged by the Striker's final hit.
Comfortable intercepts help remove Overdrive and reduce failed armor rotations.
Champions that maintain several Buffs can improve armor damage, but execution of the three armor interactions remains mandatory.

cheatSheet.objective: Hit his Block or bypass/break Auto-Block

cheatSheet.watch: A partial Striker sequence is not enough
Save major damage for this window
Ordinary attacks no longer solve the fight
Do not wait for his Light Attack

preparation: Bind a usable Striker before entering.
Learn which icon corresponds to each armor type and do not repeat an interaction while that armor is locked.
Plan to dodge Special Attacks rather than allowing Special Attack 3; Cerastes' Special Attack 3 causes an unavoidable knockout.

troubleshooting.response: You are probably repeating its interaction while it is locked. Damage a different armor type before returning to it.
Make sure the final hit of the Striker actually connects.
Do not block and wait for his Light Attack. Land your own Light Attack into Cerastes' Block to trigger the finish condition.

guideDetails.scope: Original Act 8.3.6 Cerastes fight. Crucible and other variants are outside this guide.

verification.label: Community-sourced · cross-checked
verification.note: The armor loop and final 1% interaction were re-checked. The final action is the attacker landing a Light Attack into Cerastes' Block. No current-client gameplay test is recorded.

attackerProfile: Reliable Heavy and Special Attack punishment, because damage begins from a punish opening.
A useful Striker or Special Attack Stun can extend a valid damage chain.
Comfort dodging Special Attacks is important because Wound of Defiance can punish blocked hits.

cheatSheet.watch: Normal Parry-combo play is not the damage trigger
SP1 can grant Unstoppable; SP2 can grant Unblockable

cheatSheet.objective: Survive Indestructible, then finish from a valid punish
cheatSheet.watch: Any hit during the 16-second window is lethal

preparation: Treat blocked Special Attack hits as unsafe: Wound of Defiance can deal Direct Damage through Block.
Learn the Counter-Attack Charge response before attempting long Basic Attack strings.
Do not bring a strategy that depends on your own Immortality or Indestructible; those effects can trigger a lethal Special Attack 3 response.

troubleshooting.problem: My Basic Attacks stop doing useful damage
troubleshooting.response: Re-establish a valid damage chain by dodging a Heavy or Special Attack and punishing the recovery.
Stop ordinary Basic Attacks and use the first hit of a Special Attack or Striker to remove the charge.

troubleshooting.problem: I die while blocking a Special Attack
troubleshooting.response: Wound of Defiance can trigger through Block. Practice the full dodge instead of treating Block as the safety option.

guideDetails.scope: Original Act 8.4.6 Glykhan fight across all three Health Bars and the final Indestructible window.

verification.label: Community-sourced · cross-checked
verification.note: Core damage-entry, Divine Punishment and final Indestructible mechanics were source-reviewed. No independent gameplay test is recorded.

counters.why: Community Act 8 reports specifically recommend Buff-heavy Cosmic attackers for Cerastes, and Gamora has been reported as a particularly strong fit.
counters.strategy: Use the required Leg/Shield/Spirit Armor rotation first, then spend Gamora's burst during the all-armor-broken Stun.
counters.risks: A strong damage Champion still fails if the Striker final hit misses or a locked armor interaction is repeated.
counters.scoreReason: Community-supported boss option with relevant fight fit; not independently gameplay-tested by this site.
conditions: Respect the armor lock icons before each interaction.

counters.why: A current progression report describes Chee'ilth taking Cerastes almost to a solo, making her a credible community-supported option.
counters.strategy: Follow the armor rotation exactly and use the boss-created Stun for damage rather than relying on ordinary Parry-Stun openings.
counters.risks: The final 5% sequence is execution-driven; damage output does not skip the 1% Light-Attack-into-Block finish.
counters.scoreReason: Community-supported boss option with relevant fight fit; not independently gameplay-tested by this site.
conditions: At 1%, finish by landing a Light Attack into Cerastes' Block.

counters.why: Community Act 8 counter lists call out Storm as a Glykhan option.
counters.strategy: Create damage chains by fully avoiding a Heavy or Special Attack and punishing the recovery; use Storm's damage inside those valid chains.
counters.risks: Blocked Special Attack hits can still trigger Wound of Defiance, so do not rely on Block for safety.
counters.scoreReason: Community-supported boss option with relevant fight fit; not independently gameplay-tested by this site.
conditions: Start damage from a valid punish opening.
Stop Basic Attacks when Counter-Attack Charge requires a Special Attack or Striker response.

counters.why: Storm (Pyramid X) is also specifically listed by the community as a Glykhan option.
counters.strategy: Use the same boss-first plan: punish Heavy/Special recovery to establish damage, then extend only while the chain remains valid.
counters.risks: Champion utility does not remove Glykhan's punishment system or final Indestructible survival window.
counters.scoreReason: Community-supported boss option with relevant fight fit; not independently gameplay-tested by this site.
conditions: Dodge Special Attacks rather than blocking them.
Disengage during the final Indestructible window.

counters.why: Magneto appears in community Glykhan recommendations and can provide strong damage when the boss mechanic creates a valid chain.
counters.strategy: Build your damage around the fight's punish openings rather than attempting ordinary Parry-combo play.
counters.risks: Do not assume Magneto's kit bypasses Divine Punishment or Counter-Attack Charge.
counters.scoreReason: Community-supported boss option with relevant fight fit; not independently gameplay-tested by this site.
conditions: Use a valid Heavy/Special punish to start damage.
Respect Counter-Attack Charge and the final Indestructible timer.
